description: Service configuration for the /v1 surface. Spec II.10: nothing site-, vehicle- or criteria-dependent is hard-coded in source, and rate limits and timeouts are configuration values rather than literals (spec IV.8).

service.default_criteria_version_source: spec II.10 launch commit criteria row names data/criteria_v1.json. WEATHER owns that file; while it is absent the API falls back to the version string configured here and records in the log that no criteria rows were read.
service.default_raan_tolerance_source: spec IV.1 says the RAAN tolerance default is per target class but does not tabulate the values. ENGINE owns them, so the API passes null through and never invents one.

LEO.source: spec IV.1 type mapping: LEO resolves to the configured default, the 45.1 deg advertised class; altitude is the row of the spec III drift table for that class

POLAR.source: spec IV.1 type mapping: POLAR resolves to an inclination in the band 87.9 to 90.0 deg, nominal 87.9 deg; altitude is the row of the spec III drift table for that class

SSO.source: spec IV.1 type mapping: SSO resolves to about 98.1 deg, derived from the target altitude by the spec II.6 inclination table unless i_t is given; the class altitude is the SSO-consistent row of the spec III drift table

sso.inclination_table_source: spec II.6 altitude-inclination coupling table, computed from the mean motion relation with the spec II.10 constants
sso.required_nodal_rate_source: spec II.6: the SSO inclination is the solution of the nodal drift relation at a mean Sun rate of 0.9856 deg/day (SCIENCE eq. A5)
sso.consistency_tolerance_source: half of the coarsest precision the spec II.6 table is quoted at, 97.8 deg to one decimal. Beyond it the requested inclination cannot be told apart from the required one at the precision the specification publishes.
sso.reachable_min_inclination_source: not applicable: direct ascent reaches every inclination at or above the site latitude, spec II.4 and spec II.9

fixture_inclination_tolerance_source: The published inclination table spans 1.6 deg across its 500 to 900 km range, so a frozen row counts as describing a resolved target whose inclination lies within half of that span of the row value. Rows outside the band are not echoed for another orbit class; that class gets the empty result spec IV.1 defines, which is informative rather than wrong.
retry_after_source: spec IV.7 rule 2 requires Retry-After on 429 and on 503. The values are configuration; no test asserts a particular duration, only the header is present and positive.
fixtures_note: Spec V.5 offline fallback: precomputed documents shipped in the repository, served when a live layer is unavailable. Spec V.5 also asks for them to be generated by a script from a real engine run; until ENGINE lands they are hand-frozen copies of the frozen contract examples, and every response built from them carries engine_version stub.
